claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances and the child or children you're enquiring about.

Let's start: **How many children are you enquiring about, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking into claiming Child Benefit for my son Alex. He's 21 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 21 years old, Child Benefit eligibility depends on whether he is in approved education or training. Let me ask you about his current situation:

**Is Alex currently in full-time, non-advanced education (such as A-levels, Scottish Highers, or NVQs up to level 3) or approved training (such as an unpaid traineeship)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not studying at the moment. He finished his education a while back.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

I need to read the official guidance to confirm the eligibility rules, but based on what you've told me, I can share the outcome with you.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Based on the official guidance, I now have enough information to provide you with a decision about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid you would **not be eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why:

**For Alex (age 21):**
- Child Benefit is normally available for children under 16 years old
- For children aged 16 or over, you can only continue to receive Child Benefit if they are **under 20** and remain in **approved education or training**
- Since Alex is 21 years old and is no longer in education, he does not meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit

Unfortunately, once a child reaches 20 years of age, Child Benefit stops regardless of their education status, and since Alex is 21 and not in education, he falls outside the qualifying age range.

If you have any other questions or if your circumstances change, please don't hesitate to ask.

reasonings: Alex is 21 years old and is not currently in approved education or training. According to the Child Benefit eligibility rules, you can normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16. For children aged 16 or over, you'll normally still qualify only if the child is under 20 AND they stay in approved education or training. Since Alex is 21 (over the age of 20) and is no longer in education, he does not meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit.
arguments.overall_reasoning: The claimant is not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex because he is 21 years old and no longer in approved education or training. Child Benefit can only be claimed for children under 16, or for those aged 16-19 who remain in approved education or training. Alex exceeds both the age limit and is not in qualifying education.
